text: Why is the information measure a logarithm rather than, say, 1/p?
choices: Information from independent events must add, while their probabilities multiply — and the logarithm is the function that converts one into the other.
Because the measure must be zero at p = 0, which 1/p is not.
Because a bit is defined as a base-2 quantity, and only a logarithm is base-dependent.
Because logarithms are bounded, so no single event can carry infinite information.
explanation: Two coin flips should be two bits, not one and not four. p(two heads) = 1/4, and -log₂(1/4) = 2. The base-2 choice is what makes the unit a bit; base e gives nats and base 10 gives hartleys, differing by a constant factor. Note also that an impossible event carries infinite information under this measure, which is why it does not happen.
